$comment: Fixed inputs and the one signature they produce, so an implementation can check itself without a round trip. The message signed is the timestamp, a dot, then the raw body bytes — the timestamp is inside the signature so a captured body cannot be moved forward to keep it fresh. The expected value was computed independently in Python's hmac and in `openssl dgst -sha256 -mac HMAC`, and both agreed with the application's own implementation. If this number ever changes, the algorithm has changed, and every implementation built against the old one starts failing at the door.
message: <timestamp> + "." + <body>, as bytes, with no trailing newline

headers.X-Key-Id: the id of the key used, from the agreed allow-list
